## Why This Is Asked
Multi-tenant logging can cause IO contention and latency spikes when many small writers share a single path. This question tests practical isolation, rotation, and QoS strategies without changing app code.

## Key Concepts
- Systemd sandboxing: PrivateTmp, PrivateDevices, ReadOnlyPaths
- Per-tenant log isolation and rotation using logrotate
- Disk I/O control: ionice and IO scheduling
- Quotas: per-tenant quotas on a dedicated log volume (e.g., project quotas on XFS)
- Test plan: simulate bursts and verify rollback safety

## Code Example
```ini
; /etc/systemd/system/ci-agent@.service
[Unit]
Description=CI Agent for tenant %i

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/ci-agent --tenant=%i
PrivateTmp=true
PrivateDevices=true
ReadOnlyPaths=/var/log/ci
AmbientCapabilities=CAP_SYSLOG
IOSchedulingClass=idle
IOSchedulingPriority=7
```

```bash
; /etc/logrotate.d/ci-agent-%i
/var/log/ci/tenant-*/agent.log {
  size 50M
  rotate 7
  copytruncate
  missingok
  notifempty
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate per-tenant isolation under peak bursts? 
- Which metrics would you monitor to detect drift or misconfigurations, and how would you roll back safely?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Security-critical deployments require verifiable runtime integrity. This tests knowledge of kernel integrity (IMA), secure deployment workflows, and integration with systemd and CI.

## Key Concepts
- Linux IMA and runtime attestation
- Signed binaries in CI and secure repositories
- systemd integration (ExecStartPre) and rollback mechanisms
- Tamper-detection tests and observability

## Code Example
```bash
# validate-binaries.sh (conceptual)
set -euo pipefail
EXPECTED_HASH=$(cat /etc/ci/signatures/service.sha256)
ACTUAL_HASH=$(sha256sum /usr/local/bin/myservice | awk '{print $1}')
if [ "$ACTUAL_HASH" != "$EXPECTED_HASH" ]; then
  echo "Signature mismatch" >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/myservice.service (snippet)
[Unit]
Description=My Critical Service

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/myservice
ExecStartPre=/usr/local/bin/validate-binaries.sh
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle CI/CD with multiple binary variants across environments?
- How would you monitor and alert on attestation failures in production?

## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses practical expertise in storage isolation and virtualization with shared PMEM, requiring concrete, actionable solutions rather than abstract concepts.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant I/O control with cgroup v2 and quotas
- PMEM and NUMA awareness for latency-sensitive workloads
- Filesystem tuning for high-throughput shared storage
- Observability tooling: iostat, blktrace, perf
- Canary rollout and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```bash
# Example baseline commands
# Set per-tenant I/O throttling (cgroup v2)
echo "8:0 rbps=max wbps=max riops=max wiops=max" > /sys/fs/cgroup/<tenant>/io.max

# Pin container to CPU cores and NUMA node
echo "0-7" > /sys/fs/cgroup/<tenant>/cpuset.cpus
echo "0" > /sys/fs/cgroup/<tenant>/cpuset.mems

# XFS filesystem tuning for PMEM
mkfs.xfs -d su=2m,sw=1 -m reflink=0,dax /dev/pmem0
mount -o dax,noatime,nodiratime /dev/pmem0 /mnt/pmem
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate no regressions across tenant workloads after implementing I/O limits?
- What monitoring alerts would indicate impending tail latency issues?
- How do you handle tenant churn (container creation/destruction) with cgroup v2 policies?

## Why This Is Asked

Assesses practical use of hardware-assisted isolation (Intel RDT) and OS-enforced resource controls to tame tail latency under bursty, multi-tenant workloads on NUMA systems.

- cpuset/memcg: enforce CPU/memory isolation per tenant
- pqos, perf, pidstat: observability for validation
- Rollback plan: safe revert if QoS degrades

## Code Example

```bash
# Illustrative commands (adjust ranges per system)
sudo pqos -R
# Partition L3 cache: cores 0-3 -> tenantA, 4-7 -> tenantB
sudo pqos -e "L3:0=0xF;L3:1=0xF0"
# Assign tasks by user/org (replace with real PIDs)
sudo pqos -a "u:tenantA=0-3;u:tenantB=4-7"
```

- How would you handle tenant migration or hardware failures affecting MBA/L3CA partitions?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design end-to-end latency isolation on a single host using NUMA awareness, kernel boot parameters, IRQ affinity, and precise cgroup isolation. It examines practical trade-offs between throughput, isolation, and complexity.

## Key Concepts
- NUMA-aware CPU/Memory Placement
- Kernel isolation: isolcpus, nohz_full, and CPU shielding
- IRQ affinity and CPU sets in a cgrouped environment
- cgroup v2: cpu.max, io.max, memory.high, memlock
- Latency testing: fio burst I/O and cyclictest tail latency

## Code Example
```bash
# Example: create a dedicated NUMA node and isolate a slice
# 1) Isolate CPUs 2-5 on NUMA node 1
sudo isolcpus=2-5 nohz_full=2-5 bootparams
# 2) Create critical.slice and assign limits
systemd-run --unit=critical.slice --slice=critical.slice --property=CPUQuota=25%
# 3) Bind ingestion process to the slice and CPUs
taskset -c 2-5 ./ingest_service
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this plan to a multi-node cluster with live failover?
- Which monitoring hooks (perf, ftrace, iostat, pidstat) would you wire for ongoing validation?

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses practical resource isolation under multi-tenant load using modern cgroup2 controls and robust rollback strategies.

## Key Concepts
- cgroups v2 memory controls: memory.max, memory.swap.max, memory.high
- Per-tenant slices with CPU pinning and I/O throttling
- OOMScoreAdjust tuning, swap minimization, burst handling
- Fair reclaim algorithms and page-cache pressure management

## Code Example
```bash
# Create per-tenant slice with memory limits
systemd-run --slice=tenant-A.slice \
  --property=MemoryMax=2G \
  --property=MemorySwapMax=1G \
  --property=MemoryHigh=1.8G \
  --property=CPUQuota=50% \
  --property=IOReadBandwidthMax="/dev/sda 10M" \
  --property=IOWriteBandwidthMax="/dev/sda 10M" \
  /usr/bin/docker run --rm tenant-workload

# Configure OOM score adjustment
echo 500 > /proc/$(pidof tenant-workload)/oom_score_adj
echo -1000 > /proc/$(pidof systemd)/oom_score_adj
```

## Test Plan
- Deploy synthetic tenants with varying memory profiles
- Simulate burst scenarios with stress testing tools
- Monitor swap usage, OOM events, and latency metrics
- Validate rollback path via systemd slice removal
